newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance minister vows again to defend baht.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance minister vows again to defend baht.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Monday repeated a vow to defend the baht currency and maintain its stability by keeping the current exchange rate system.

"We remain convinced that our actions to defend the baht and maintain its stability are premised on sound economic principles, and not on national pride," Amnuay said in remarks prepared for a speech to international business leaders.
"We have never doubted that this is the correct approach, and I can assure you that this policy will continue well into the future," he said.
Amnuay said the baht has benefited and remained stable because of the way it is fixed against a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.

"The present exchange rate system has been the anchor of growth and stability for the past 13 years and has helped to encourage steady foreign direct investment inflows," he said. "The system is sound, credible and sustainable."
Over the past few months the baht has been hit by several rounds of rumours of a possible devaluation and speculative attacks by investors. The central bank has repeatedly ruled out a devaluation.
